| Category = Bread recipes
| Time = 30 minutes
| Difficulty = 1
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Baghrir''' are a variety of small, spongy [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancake]] or [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] popular in North Africa, including Algeria. They are made of semolina and/or all-purpose flour, and they are characteristically laced with tiny holes that soak up whatever sauce they are served with. The recipe is quick, simple, and uncomplicated.

== Ingredients ==

* 2½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|plain flour]]
* 15 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] instant [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 15 g white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 7 g table [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
* 4 cups warm water
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]

== Procedure ==

# Combine the semolina, flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
# Mix in the water and egg until you get a smooth [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]]. 
# Set batter aside, and let rest for 15–20 minutes or until doubled in size.
# Thin with a little water if necessary, then [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] in the baking powder.
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat.
# Lightly grease the skillet, then dollop in enough batter to make a few small pancakes.
# Cook the pancakes on one side until the top is covered in holes and fully cooked. Do not flip and cook on the second side.
# Remove baghrir from the pan, and repeat the cooking process with any remaining batter.
# Serve with butter.
